headline: ZOZO and Marui Group disclosed large exposures tied to the same KARTE breach, and Peach Aviation reported nearly 9 million records exposed in a separate vendor incident. CNN reported an apparent intrusion into the FBI’s national crime database, which the agency has not publicly confirmed.

incidents.what: ZOZO confirmed customer data exposure through KARTE. The ZOZOTOWN and WEAR counts may overlap; passwords and payment cards were not affected.
Marui Group confirmed that unauthorized access at marketing vendor PLAID exposed Marui retail and Epos Card data.
incidents.scale: 8.83M Marui records and 8.5M Epos records; not a unique-person count

incidents.what: Peach disclosed that an October intrusion at email vendor Yumirulink affected customer records. Passport and card information was not involved.
Sales after a deployer-account compromise drove XMR1 down to about $1. Wagyu attributed the compromise to its hosting provider; the link has not been independently established.
incidents.scale: About $13.5M in sales, not a new loss this run

incidents.what: Reuters relayed CNN’s report of an investigation into apparent unauthorized access to the national crime database and said the FBI did not respond to its request for comment.
CISA confirmed that attackers are exploiting a vulnerability in SAP NetWeaver.
incidents.scale: Known exploited vulnerability; victim count not disclosed

incidents.what: Universeum told guests that an attack on booking supplier Visit Group International exposed contact information.
incidents.scale: About 280,000 contact records; no payment data reported exposed

incidents.what: Illinois disclosed an investigation into an apparent cyberattack at Algonquin Dam. The dam remained operational, and officials have not confirmed a compromise.
WOW WORLD confirmed that unauthorized access to service servers exposed information it held for four clients.
The think tank told donors that an October intrusion at its online donations vendor exposed some contact information.
Pelayo reported unauthorized access to personal data, including policy records and bank account identifiers for some customers.
RIKEN published an updated scope assessment and asked potentially affected users to revoke and replace credentials found on the supercomputer.
